clue.text: After prayer, I have growing concern for socialist experiment

parts.note: a collect is a short prayer in the Anglican liturgy
I have contracts to I've
a farm is a business that grows crops, a punning concern

explanation.surface: A believer, after praying, takes up a farming venture as part of a socialist scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just sets the order: the prayer comes first. 'Growing concern' puns on 'going concern'.
explanation.definitionFit: Soviet-style collectivised agriculture was a defining socialist venture, pooling land and labour.

clue.text: Curiously random occurrence blocking fuel

indicators.note: the word for occurrence sits inside the fuel word, blocking it

parts.note: coal is a solid fuel
an incident is an event or occurrence

explanation.surface: An odd chance event causes a blockage in the fuel supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curiously random occurrence' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'random'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something coincidental happens by chance, curiously lining up with something else.

clue.text: Wretch in peasant garb removing top

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: a peasant blouse is a loose smock-like top

explanation.surface: A miserable figure in rustic clothing takes off an outer layer.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a louse means they are a contemptible person, a wretch.

clue.text: Parent's half as old as us — following?

indicators.note: only the second half of the word parent is used here

parts.note: something as old as us is of our age

explanation.surface: A puzzled child wonders whether a parent is half their own age, or whether that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A following is a group of attendants or supporters around a notable person, an entourage.

clue.text: Beat given by instrument, no favourite, creating a storm

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them

indicators.note: no signals that the favourite is dropped from the instrument

parts.note: a trumpet is a brass instrument
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A child, denied a favourite toy instrument, beats it and kicks up a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is an outburst of temper, a storm of rage.

clue.text: One answering for token

definitions.meaning: someone who vouches for another answers for them

explanation.definitionFit: One who vouches is a guarantor; a gift voucher is a token.

clue.text: War zone that is right away from country's boundary

indicators.note: these letters are taken away from the boundary word

parts.note: a frontier is a national border

explanation.surface: A combat zone lies just off the national border.
explanation.definitionFit: The front is the line where opposing armies meet in combat.

clue.text: Poor infrastructure not affected by storms

indicators.note: the second half of infrastructure asks for the letters before it to be built into a new structure

parts.note: the first part of infrastructure is used as written

explanation.surface: Shoddy public works never seem to cope with bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word infrastructure does double duty: its front half is fodder and its back half signals the rebuild.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weatherproof against rain is unaffected by storms.

clue.text: One night in Quebec for this Canadian

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
nuit is French for night, the language of Quebec

explanation.surface: A traveller spends a night in Quebec with a Canadian.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit are indigenous people of Arctic Canada.

clue.text: Nurses' leader notes one's worrying condition

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: euros are banknotes of the European currency
one is gives I + IS

explanation.surface: A head nurse writes notes about a patient's troubling ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosis is a mental disorder marked by anxiety and worry.

clue.text: Hence unlucky casualties from the smiling assassin?

definitions.text: Hence unlucky casualties from the smiling assassin?

parts.words: Hence unlucky casualties from the smiling assassin?
parts.note: an assassin who smiles is friendly, so the shots he fires are friendly shots that hit his own side

explanation.definitionFit: Accidental shots on one's own troops by allies, causing unlucky casualties.

clue.text: In country house, endless draught

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: Chequers is the British Prime Minister's country residence in Buckinghamshire

explanation.surface: A draughty old country house always lets the wind in.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is a piece in the board game draughts, also called a chequer.

clue.text: Percy's resistance to push for change in advance

definitions.note: Percy is: the clue's 's links the name to the wordplay

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Percy resists being pushed into paying for change up front.
explanation.walkthrough: R placed in advance of TO PUSH gives the letters to change. Sir Henry Percy, nicknamed Hotspur, is the rebel in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotspur was the nickname of the medieval nobleman Sir Henry Percy.

clue.text: Had a chance to secure a place in the country

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer within it, as if securing it

explanation.surface: Someone had the opportunity to buy a rural property.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country cottage or second home.

clue.text: Opening menu, I don't go first for gristle

indicators.note: the menu word is opened up so other letters can go in

parts.note: a carte is a menu, as in a la carte
to lag is to fall behind rather than lead

explanation.surface: A diner opens the menu, but holds back from ordering the gristly dish first.
explanation.definitionFit: Gristle is tough cartilage found in meat.

clue.text: Extra rules around initialised Short Message System

indicators.note: the extra word goes around the initial letter

parts.note: more means extra

indicators.note: initialised means reduced to its initial letter

parts.note: a code is a set of rules

explanation.surface: Further regulations apply to the SMS texting service.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue mimics SMS, Short Message Service, but 'Short' is only wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The dot-dash telegraph system devised by Samuel Morse sends messages.

clue.text: Duck out of sight, perhaps, in cover

parts.note: an eider is a sea duck
something gone down, like a setting sun, may be out of sight

explanation.surface: A duck ducks out of sight and hides under cover.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt or bed cover, originally stuffed with eider feathers.

clue.text: Carer's surname mistakenly given to papers

definitions.note: carer is: the 's joins the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the letters are set out wrongly, so rearranged

parts.note: ID is identity papers

explanation.surface: A carer's surname is wrongly entered on official documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny employed to look after children is a carer.

clue.text: Learns a remarkable stock of insults

indicators.note: remarkable suggests the letters are made into something else

explanation.surface: Someone builds up an impressive supply of insults.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a store of weapons, figuratively any stockpile, here of jibes.

clue.text: From pills, died in front of shareholders

indicators.note: in a down clue this puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: shareholders are part owners of a company

explanation.surface: A shareholder died after taking pills.
explanation.definitionFit: Downers are slang for depressant drugs such as sedative tablets.

clue.text: Finally retired, challenge to return for former county

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter
to return means read backwards

parts.note: to defy is to challenge

explanation.surface: Having finally retired, a challenge is issued to go back to the old county.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyfed was a Welsh administrative county from 1974 to 1996.

clue.text: Gets down article with one's knowledge

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
one's lights are one's understanding, as in according to one's lights

explanation.surface: Someone climbs down from a vehicle carrying a book and their learning.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to step off a vehicle, to get down.

clue.text: Poem from WWI leader almost upset country

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Douglas Haig commanded British forces on the Western Front in WWI

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A war poem about a First World War general who nearly toppled the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a short Japanese poem of three lines.

clue.text: Lazy, but is successful and extremely happy

parts.note: a plan that works is successful

indicators.note: extremely picks the extreme letters, first and last

explanation.surface: An idle person who still succeeds and is very content.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone work-shy avoids effort, being idle by nature.

clue.text: Some terrific stories turned up in this

definitions.text: Some terrific stories turned up in this

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from bottom to top
some means only part of the words is used

explanation.surface: Great tales surface in science fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction is a genre where terrific stories appear, so the whole clue defines it.

clue.text: Glow from off-peak heater nice — one's out of it

indicators.note: off means the peak is removed

parts.note: a radiator is a room heater
a tor is a rocky peak, especially on Dartmoor

indicators.note: out of it means the letter is removed from the word nice

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cheap-rate storage heater gives a nice glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's out of it' reads as 'one is out of it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiance is a warm glow of light.

clue.text: Animal's bone found in bits

definitions.note: animal is: the 's links definition to wordplay

indicators.note: the bone is found inside the bits

parts.note: binary bits are 0 and 1, read as letters O and I
a rib is a bone

explanation.surface: A creature's bone turns up in fragments.
explanation.definitionFit: The oribi is a small African antelope.

clue.text: Unmixed drink quite horrible, unless air is circulated

indicators.note: horrible tells us the word quite is mangled
circulated means the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A neat spirit tastes awful in a stuffy room.
explanation.walkthrough: The cocktail is layered, not stirred, so it is fairly unmixed.
explanation.definitionFit: This cocktail of tequila, orange juice and grenadine settles into sunrise-like layers.
